pois.caption_hd: Philippines water shortages hit more than 6 million people
pois.caption_body: More than 6 million people in the Philippines have been hit by water shortages in capital Manila and nearby Rizal province. Water supply has been cut off for at least six hours each day, and authorities have appealed to hospital patients to limit visitors to reduce water use. Many water-dependent businesses have also closed temporarily. Water supplier Manila Water said water levels in dams has fallen due to the El Niño effect, while the government has been blamed for decades-long delays to new dam construction projects.

event_desc: During an El Niño event, Hong Kong generally experiences a noticeable shift in climate patterns, typically characterized by fewer tropical cyclones and below-average rainfall. Because the phenomenon causes typhoons in the western North Pacific to form further east, these storms are more likely to track northward toward Japan or Korea rather than making landfall near the South China coast. Additionally, El Niño tends to weaken the southwest monsoon over the South China Sea, cutting off the vital moisture supply to southern China and resulting in unseasonably dry weather, particularly during the late summer and autumn months.

pois.caption_hd: Record floods caused catastrophic damage to infrastructure in the state of Queensland, Australia
pois.caption_body: Driven by a historic La Niña, the 2010–2011 floods plunged eastern Australia into an unprecedented crisis, leaving an area larger than France and Germany underwater. Queensland bore the brunt of the disaster, where torrential rains triggered a deadly inland tsunami in the Lockyer Valley and submerged entire suburbs of Brisbane, the state's capital.

pois.caption_body: Sri Lanka suffered massive blows to its agricultural sector, losing approximately 20 to 30 percent of its vital winter rice crop to the submerging floodwaters. This catastrophic damage severely crippled rural livelihoods, threatened national food security, and ultimately forced Sri Lanka to rely on emergency food imports to stabilize skyrocketing domestic market prices.

pois.caption_hd: Birds fly over the Old Parana River, a tributary of the Parana River, during a drought in Argentina
pois.caption_body: Fueled by a rare three-year La Niña, Argentina’s worst drought in over six decades caused a catastrophic collapse in agricultural yields during 2021 to 2023, with soybean production plunging by over 40% and corn output contracting by 25%. The crisis resulted in an estimated $20 billion in direct economic losses, slashing the nation's critical export revenues by over 40%.
